chapter_theme: A song at Thiruchaththimuththam (திருச்சத்திமுத்தம்): the poet describes women's breasts and wandering eyes and asks to stop suffering in their grip; the praise names Murugan who taught the meaning of the Veda to Siva and confounds the fools who live by lies and plunder of the simple.

875.reading: The poet describes women's breasts, compared to elephant tusks, golden pots and lotus buds and smeared with fragrant paste, and their kayal-fish eyes leaping to the earrings and their hard words, and asks whether he will not cease to suffer, pressed in the grip of these women. The praise names Murugan who told the meaning of the rare Veda to three-eyed Siva and drove the peacock round the world in an instant, the hero who confounds and cuts down the fools who tell lies, heap up wealth and frighten simple people to make their living, the nephew of Vishnu who sleeps on the serpent and came swiftly on Garuda, and the lord who cut the one in the sea with his shakti, at Thiruchaththimuththam.
875.nuance: அபகடம் உரைத்து அத்தம் மெத்தப் படைத்து உலகில் எளியரை மருட்டி ... அசடர்: an unusual target for Murugan's wrath, not demons but men who grow rich by deceiving the simple. அடலை புனை முக்கண் பரற்குப் பொருள் சொல் அருமறை: the teaching of Siva, here of the Veda's meaning without naming Om. The second half of the plea (கணியினில் அகப்பட்டு) is hard to divide.
